newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Bank of East Asia net in line, valuation seen high.
newsitem.headline: Bank of East Asia net in line, valuation seen high.

text.p: Bank of East Asia Ltd's 1996 net profit came in largely in line with estimates, but analysts said on Monday that the bank's earnings growth did not warrant its current price earnings ratio.

"The results are OK -- a bit above expectations -- but I am not positive," said Alan Hutcheson, director of research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. "It is basically the most expensive bank in Hong Kong."

Bank of East Asia posted 1996 net profit of HK$1.88 billion, including an exceptional gain of HK$28.27 million from the sale of property, compared with HK$1.64 billion. Analysts said the bank's shares were trading at around 20 times earnings.
The stock fell HK$1.00 on Monday to close at HK$33.90.

"People think the stock does not deserve to be trading at a premium to almost every bank. You can buy much smaller companies trading at a lower PE and with higher growth rates," said Percy Au-Young, director of research at DBS Securities.
Analysts said Bank of East Asia's exposure to China had prompted investors to pay a premium for the stock.
Bank of East Asia increased its network in the mainland to 11 branches and representative offices in 1996 after opening a Tianjin representative office in June.

"You are paying a pretty steep premium for the China business and there is some concern that profitability of the China business is not as good as it could be," said Shannon Garrett, banking analyst at SocGen-Crosby Securities.
"The China business is expanding but you are not seeing comparable growth in profit growth, meaning they are being too conservative or seeing margin pressure," she added.
Garrett said the bank's net interest margin had been disappointing and Bank of East Asia had seen a decline in market share in the mortgage market.

Bank of East Asia said its interest margin in 1996 was 2.97 percent compared with 2.92 percent the previous year. It said mortgages grew 17 percent while advances to customers grew 23.8 percent to HK$64.17 billion.
However, analysts said they were positive about Bank of East Asia's 26.6 percent rise in non-interest income to HK$961.59 million.

"They have probably reached the ceiling in terms of exposure to the mortgage market and are looking at the next growth story which is consumer finance," said Steven Thompson, chief analyst at Nikko Securities.
Bank of East Asia said mortgages represented about 45 percent of its total loan portfolio.
Thompson said he expected net profit growth of about 17-18 percent in 1997.
"They will not have any exceptionals from property -- they will only book property income in 1998 -- so growth will not be that much," said Alex Wong, analyst at Dharmala Securities.
He predicted 1997 net profit of HK$2.1 billion.
"After that, I think in 1998 the growth will pick up again. I think in 1998 they will again have income booked from property development," said Wong.
